summary: King Leopold II of Belgium used sham philanthropic associations and fraudulent treaties to make the Congo Free State his personal property, then ran it as a forced-labor rubber operation that killed millions while he bought favorable press.

evidence.note: birth and childhood of Leopold covered
1876 Brussels Geographic Conference launches the sham African association
extended segment on Stanley's violent expeditions and treaty gathering
successive look-alike philanthropic fronts used to mislead donors and public
labor taxes enforced with hostage camps for rubber quotas
hands-for-bullets policy and village massacres described
Leopold's international PR campaign: paid journalists, bought editors
long segment on his teenage mistress Caroline, later Baroness Vaughan
Leopold dies December 1909 after handing Congo to Belgium in 1908
Belgian home politics: 1902 general strike shooting

notes: Primary theme could be genocide-mass-killing (taxonomy example lists Leopold there); chose colonialism since the pitch is how he acquired and exploited a colony. Part 2 coda on colonial whipping (Putumayo, Belgian Congo to 1945, Mau Mau in Kenya) is short and not about Leopold, so excluded from span and setting. main_span starts at the 1876 conference rather than accession in 1865.
